title: Reverse Engineering Anything using small open models
gist: Hugging Face tests a lead-plus-small-workers agent swarm (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash lead, Qwen3.5-9B workers) at reverse engineering compiled binaries into Python. The team approach was slower and costlier on a 38-function task but tied the solo run on cost at 56 functions, with about 40% of functions still needing the lead.

insights.claim: A reverse-engineering pipeline can pair one capable lead model (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) with small open worker models (Qwen3.5-9B) that pull tasks from a shared board and verify rewrites against a ~600-case diff_test oracle before submitting.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Test-oracle-gated small-model swarms are a template for cheap agentic code translation; watch for adoption in legacy-code migration tooling.

insights.claim: Workers whose attempts fail repeatedly escalate the function to the lead agent, which then takes the task on itself, making the lead the fallback for hard cases.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Escalation rate is the key cost driver of hierarchical agent systems; track it as a metric.

insights.claim: The lead agent is allowed to modify the workers' harnesses (system prompts, new tools), which lets the team's scaffolding evolve during a run.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Self-improving scaffolds are an emerging pattern; the harness may matter more than the model.

insights.claim: On the 38-function Hugging Face logo task, the lead-plus-4-workers team was slower and more expensive than a solo DeepSeek agent: $2.97 and 86 minutes versus $0.87 and 14 minutes.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: For small tasks, multi-agent orchestration with small models is a net cost loss; do not assume swarms are cheaper.

insights.claim: On the 56-function space shooter task, the team cost $3.60 versus $3.28 for the solo agent, so costs converged, while the solo agent needed 4 launches and 54 minutes and the team needed 2 launches and 100 minutes.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: The crossover point where small-model swarms match solo large-model cost appears to move with task size.

insights.claim: In absolute cost the pipeline starts to tie with the solo run as the number of functions rises, and a solo agent struggles to handle the bigger task in one long run.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Decomposable long-horizon work is where hierarchical agents may pay off; two data points only.
insights.quote: A solo run struggles handling this big task in a single long run.

insights.claim: About 40% of functions needed escalation to the lead (15 of 38 on the logo task, 20 of 56 on the shooter), so small workers alone do not suffice.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: The small-model share of work is capped near 60% in this setup, limiting the savings from swapping in cheap models.

insights.claim: Workers repeatedly failed draw_particles because they read AArch64 b.ls/b.hi as signed comparisons, when they are unsigned; the lead fixed it by editing the workers' system prompt instead of rewriting the function itself.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Failure-pattern diagnosis by a supervisor agent that updates worker instructions is a leverage point in agent systems.

insights.claim: The lead made three harness changes (two worker prompt revisions and a new lookup tool) after observing workers invent helper names, miscount callee arguments, and hand-derive field offsets incorrectly.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Small models fail in systematic, correctable ways; supervised prompt patching may be more valuable than larger worker models.

insights.claim: In the HF logo task the lead proposed no harness changes, possibly because the problem was too easy for it to solve in one shot and the functions were not granular enough for the small agents.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Task granularity is a design variable; poorly scoped subtasks waste worker capacity.

insights.claim: The Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) repository has crossed 370k GitHub stars, and plugging powerful models into it lets users reverse engineer almost any modern software, with community re-implementations of Adobe products, Linux extensions and game customizations.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Easy AI-driven reverse engineering raises IP and security exposure for closed-source software vendors.
insights.quote: which crossed 370k GitHub stars as we write this blog post

insights.claim: Reverse engineering a compiled binary yields control flow, strings, symbols, linked libraries and format details, and static or dynamic analysis can also expose hardcoded secrets and memory-safety bugs.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Closed-source distribution offers weaker protection as AI agents automate disassembly analysis; security teams should strip symbols and audit for embedded secrets.
insights.locator: Reverse Engineering in the context of software engineering

insights.claim: The authors conclude that small models can produce decisive results if properly scoped and placed in the right harness, and suggest pools of workers of mixed sizes and families guided by one or several leads.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Watch for heterogeneous model-swarm frameworks as the next orchestration direction.
insights.quote: Small models are capable of producing decisive content if they are properly conditioned

insights.claim: This lead/worker protocol may suit very long-horizon tasks requiring heavy planning that can be split into granular tasks, though the correlation with function count rests on only two data points.
insights.speaker: Younes B
insights.so_what: Treat as a hypothesis; look for larger replications before betting on swarm economics.
